verdicts.trueWording: Jape, aside from its pretentiousness, is a singularly displeasing word.
verdicts.note: Raw page fetched (200, 43KB HTML). Quote is word-for-word in item 1 of 'Terrible Turns of Phrase'. The 'for joke' limb is on the page: 'Whenever he talks about someone joking around, he uses the word “jape” instead of joke.'

verdicts.trueWording: Seriously, the phrase comes up at least ten times in every book.
verdicts.note: Same raw page. Verbatim, and the antecedent phrase on the page is explicitly 'mummer's farce' ('His number one most abused phrase... mummer's farce').

verdicts.trueWording: On the whole this is admirable, but sometimes his choices are inexplicable.
verdicts.note: Quote verbatim; 'admirable' and both examples (Hodor stable boy, Reek's 'it rhymes with weak/squeak' rhymes) are on the page. The 'tedious across chapters' limb is carried by the page's parodic Hodor dialogue ('those chapters which follow that storyline frequently go like this') and the author's own on-page reply ('the Hodor gimmick occur again and again and again... repetition... which distract the reader') rather than by the word 'tedious'.

verdicts.trueWording: even by these lax standards Martin's scenes are particularly dire
verdicts.note: Same raw page, section 'And the Worst Thing Ever, the Sex Scenes'. Extraneous limb supported verbatim: 'they are obviously completely extraneous, thrown in only to titillate.'

verdicts.trueWording: But his prose holds him back from being a truly great author.
verdicts.note: Same raw page, closing paragraph. The 'despite strong storytelling' limb is supported: 'For all his talents as a creator and crafter of stories' plus praise of world building, breathless pacing and plot twists.

verdicts.trueWording: He creates textured scenes full of sounds and smells and tastes.
verdicts.note: Raw Blogspot page fetched (200, 9.4KB). Preceding sentence carries the other limb verbatim: 'He has a knack for vivid (sometimes bordering on hallucinogenic) description.'

verdicts.trueWording: But he writes pulp. There is no theme; there is no moral.
verdicts.note: Same raw page. 'no depth beneath the diversion' limb: 'Martin is good diversion, but don't look too deeply.' Note the page's own concessive is 'For all its entertainment value' (vividness is asserted a paragraph earlier), not 'For all its vividness'.

verdicts.trueWording: a strong whiff of making-it-up-as-he-goes each time Martin introduces some new... wonder
verdicts.note: Same raw page; quote verbatim and the 'each new wonder' limb is the same sentence's clause ('each time Martin introduces some new and unlikely wonder in his fantasy world').

verdicts.trueWording: If you're watching A Game of Thrones on HBO, you're forgoing the great pleasure of Martin's deft prose.
verdicts.note: Live time.com/archive/6911691 returns HTTP 406 to every UA/header set and has no Wayback capture; verified on the raw Wayback capture of the same Grossman review at its original Time URL: https://web.archive.org/web/20110711021407id_/http://www.time.com/time/arts/article/0,8599,2081774,00.html (headline 'George R.R. Martin's Dance with Dragons: A Masterpiece Worthy of Tolkien', 7 Jul 2011). Raw HTML, no summarizer.

verdicts.trueWording: Like Wagner, he gives each of his characters leitmotifs that recur and recur in their streams of thought.
verdicts.note: Same Wayback raw capture. Both cited leitmotifs appear on the page: '“You know nothing, Jon Snow”; Daenerys' theme is “If I look back I am lost”'.

verdicts.trueWording: 11 major story lines... each with its own rhythm, written in its own voice, and each playing off all the others
verdicts.note: Same Wayback raw capture; the eleven-storyline limb is explicit ('follows, by my count, 11 major story lines, as well as assorted minor ones'). The NPR version of the review drops the number, so the Time text is the right source for this limb.

verdicts.trueWording: Martin will never win a Pulitzer or a National Book Award, but his skill as a crafter of narrative exceeds that of almost any literary novelist writing today.
verdicts.note: Same Wayback raw capture. 'crafter' is the Time wording; the NPR variant of the same review reads 'orchestrator of narrative', so the quote is only verbatim against the cited Time source.

verdicts.trueWording: After five volumes Martin is, if anything, a better writer than when he started.
verdicts.note: Same Wayback raw capture. Quote verbatim; the claim drops Grossman's hedge 'if anything', which softens but does not change the assertion.

verdicts.trueWording: There is no such thing as a stock character or a cardboard village there: every person, every wood and stream and street corner has its own tale.
verdicts.note: Same Wayback raw capture; both limbs in one sentence.

verdicts.trueWording: It's an epic for a more profane, more sardonic, more ambivalent age than the one Tolkien lived in.
verdicts.note: NPR page fetched live as raw HTML (200, 42KB) at the cited URL; sentence appears in the body and again as a pull-quote. Note the Time print version of the same review reads 'more jaded' where NPR reads 'more sardonic' — the cited NPR source carries the quoted wording exactly.
